teams.heading: Jake White's Fiji end Nations Championship drought by beating Italy 21-16
teams.body: Saturday's Round 6 win at Udine's Bluenergy Stadium followed five straight defeats, the last a 43-15 loss to Ireland in which Jake White's side faded after a strong first half. Italy were disrupted before kickoff when tighthead Simone Ferrari injured his left arm, Marco Riccioni stepping up. Gonzalo Quesada said Italy had faced a side averaging ten kilos more per player, praising Fiji's individual quality and solidity, and the two teams meet again in a rematch.

teams.heading: England's 37-12 win sets record margin over the All Blacks
teams.body: Saturday's five-try win at Allianz Stadium comfortably eclipsed 2012's 38-21 as England's widest margin against New Zealand. England secured the bonus point by the 43rd minute and retained the Hillary Shield. They had 64 per cent of the ball, carried 100 times to 50 and made 551 metres to 267, while the All Blacks missed 35 tackles to nine. Steve Borthwick singled out the defence: "Somebody just said to me that New Zealand got three line breaks. That’s a phenomenal effort and the players deserve enormous credit for that."

lead.why: The Moody haka angle has already run, so the record margin and the numbers behind the rout are the fresh England story.

teams.heading: Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang forced off with apparent muscle injury in 45-17 win
teams.body: The Pau wing left just after the hour on Saturday at the Stade de France, and Rugbyrama's ratings flagged it as a poor omen for the Twickenham final against South Africa. Until then he had been faultless on the right. His early chase off a Dupont kick won a five-metre scrum, and he was bundled into touch inches short on 56 minutes. Emilien Gailleton replaced him and scored in the corner with his first ball.

lead.why: A first-choice wing's apparent muscle injury is the freshest hard news for the senior side heading into the final, and it differs from the result story already run.

teams.heading: Rob Baloucoune scores twice as Ireland edge Springboks 20-17 at Aviva
teams.body: Ireland built Saturday's 20-17 win on first-half nerve: twice they turned down easy shots at goal and cashed both chances in as tries, for Baloucoune and Rónan Kelleher, before the Ulster winger's second put them 17-10 up. Sam Prendergast's penalty made it 20-10, and Malcolm Marx's try set up a nervy final 20 minutes. RTÉ judged it Ireland's best performance of the year, and the defeat left the Springboks beaten in consecutive games for the first time in four years.

teams.heading: Quesada sees progress in 16-21 Fiji defeat, Nicotera calls scrum a weapon
teams.body: Saturday's 16-21 loss to Fiji in Udine left Italy winless, but Gonzalo Quesada rated it an improvement on the previous three matches. He pointed to more possession, longer sequences and more go-forward against a side he said averaged 10 kilos more per player. Giacomo Nicotera called the scrum a growing weapon, though the captain conceded Italy might have been braver, cashing in on situations when they could have gone for a scrum. Quesada said he does not judge a performance on the result alone, with a Fiji rematch to come.

lead.why: It is the only new item on the played result, with Quesada's and Nicotera's post-match verdicts on the 16-21 loss.

teams.heading: Liam McConnell scores hat-trick on third appearance as Scotland thrash Japan 67-5
teams.body: Saturday's 67-5 Nations Championship rout at Murrayfield brought 11 Scotland tries, and the 22-year-old Edinburgh back row was electrifying in attack and defence, adding his second and third before the hour. BBC Scotland's Tom English wrote of significant frustration among his supporters at his lack of Scotland opportunities. Darcy Graham also scored three, taking his national record to 41 tries, while Gregor Townsend kept it simple: "Liam [McConnell] stands out for his tries."

lead.why: A rookie's hat-trick in only his third appearance is the new Scotland story from the 67-5 win, distinct from the Fagerson injury edition already run.

teams.heading: Wales lose 26-29 to Australia as Costelow's missed conversion proves costly
teams.body: A week after beating the All Blacks, Wales were twice 12 points down in Cardiff before Blair Murray's converted try put them 21-19 ahead on 54 minutes; Australia's 29-26 win came through Len Ikitau's try and a Carter Gordon penalty. Ryan Elias was driven over in the 79th minute, but Sam Costelow's conversion miss — his first off the tee in a Wales jersey this year — left them needing a try, and the final attack died on a forward pass. Japan await in the ninth-place final.

lead.why: The result itself is the day's most-covered new Wales story and has not yet led an edition.

teams.heading: Federico Aramburu's son sings anthem with Pumas before 45-17 Paris defeat
teams.body: Santiago, the seven-year-old son of the late Puma Federico Aramburu, walked out at the Stade de France hand in hand with both captains before Saturday's 45-17 defeat by France, then sang the anthem alongside the Argentina players in a No. 13 Pumas shirt worn in his father's honour. The 80,000 crowd had observed a minute's silence during the warm-up. Aramburu, a 22-cap Puma who played for Biarritz, was killed in Paris in March 2022; two men were sentenced in September to 26 and 19 years; both have appealed.

lead.why: The Aramburu tribute is a new Argentina story from Paris, distinct from the match report already run.

teams.heading: Carter Gordon's late penalty seals 29-26 Wallabies win and ends losing run
teams.body: Australia beat Wales 29-26 in Cardiff on Saturday, but only after surrendering the lead when Blair Murray's converted try put the hosts 21-19 up in the 54th minute. Len Ikitau restored the advantage 10 minutes later, and Carter Gordon's penalty seven minutes from time stretched it to two scores — the cushion that mattered once Ryan Elias was driven over in the 79th and Sam Costelow missed the conversion. Wales's final attack died on a forward pass, ending a four-match Wallabies losing streak.

teams.heading: Harada and Stolberg sin-binned as Japan's Murrayfield defeat ends 67-5
teams.body: Japan's 67-5 Nations Championship defeat by Scotland on Saturday brought two yellow cards for replacements: Mamoru Harada for a 69th-minute hip drop and Michael Stolberg for an early tackle in the 79th. Takuro Matsunaga's unconverted try on 53 minutes, after a box kick bounced awkwardly past Kyle Rowe, was the only Japanese score. Eddie Jones had rung wholesale changes after the 78-15 hammering by England. His side still trailed 29-0 at the break against a largely second-string Scotland, who ran in 11 tries.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett scores on 150th Test as England inflict record 37-12 defeat
teams.body: England's 37-12 win at Twickenham on Saturday was their biggest over New Zealand, eclipsing the 17-point margin of 2012's 38-21, and the All Blacks have never lost by more to northern-hemisphere opposition. Barrett, the fourth man to reach 150 Tests, rounded off a coast-to-coast try converted by Damian McKenzie to make it 24-12 on 55 minutes; Ethan de Groot had the other. The BBC suggested a long season, including four Tests against South Africa, may be catching up with the tourists a week after the shock loss to Wales.

lead.why: The record losing margin and Barrett's 150th Test are the New Zealand angles the third-place-final edition did not cover.

teams.heading: Springboks lose 20-17 in Dublin despite scrum dominance and Malcolm Marx try
teams.body: Ireland's 20-17 win at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday rested on two first-half penalties they declined in favour of the corner, turned into tries for Rob Baloucoune and Rónan Kelleher. The Bok scrum still dominated, and Morné van den Berg's try plus five points from Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu kept the visitors in touch at the break. Malcolm Marx answered Sam Prendergast's penalty with a try, and the losing bonus point was enough to beat New Zealand to top spot in the south.
